rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion For Reconsideration Of The Court'S May 27, 2026 Order Re: Allocation Of Discovery Referee Costs; Memornadum Of Points And Authorities
rulings.Rulings: Matter on the LAW AND MOTION / DISCOVERY Calendar for Thursday, JUL-30-2026. LINE 4. PLAINTIFFS MARIANGEL AGUILAR, AN INDIVIDUAL, ELENA VALENCIA, NATALY GONZALEZ, and JOSSELYN ESPINAL'S Motion For Reconsideration Of The Court'S May 27, 2026 Order Re: Allocation Of Discovery Referee Costs. Plaintiffs Ariangel Aguilar, Elena Valencia, Nataly Gonzalez and Josselyn Espinal's Motion For Reconsideration Of The Court's May 27, 2026 Order Re: Allocation Of Discovery Referee Costs is DENIED. Code of Civil Procedure section 1008(a) permits reconsideration of a prior order when the moving party shows "new or different facts, circumstances, or law" and explains why the new or different facts, circumstances, or law were not presented earlier with reasonable diligence. (New York Times Co. v. Superior Court (2005) 135 Cal.App.4th 206, 208.) "The party making the application shall state by affidavit what application was made before, when and to what judge, what order or decisions were made, and what new or different facts, circumstances, or law are claimed to be shown." (Code of Civil Procedure section 1008(a).) Plaintiffs have not identified new or different facts, circumstances or law that could not have been presented earlier with reasonable diligence that justifies reconsideration of the court's 5/27/2026 Order. The court ordered referee costs presumptively split equally between Kim Legal, APC and Defendant Short Story, authorized the referee to recommend a different allocation based on positions, responsibility or fault and noted that those costs could be reallocated at the end of the case. Plaintiffs' evidence regarding their individual ability or inability to pay is irrelevant given the court did not order them to pay any portion of the referee's costs. rulings.Case Title: JANE DOE VS. DISCORD, INC. ET AL
rulings.Rulings: Matter on the LAW AND MOTION / DISCOVERY Calendar for Thursday, JUL-30-2026. LINE 9. DEFENDANT META PLATFORMS, INC.'s Partially Unopposed Motion To Sever. Defendant Meta Platform Inc.'s motion to sever is DENIED. "[S]tatutes relating to joinder like section 378 should be liberally construed, unless expressly forbidden, to the end that a multiplicity of suits may be prevented. Consistent with this presumption in favor of joinder, a right to relief arises from the same transaction or occurrence under section 378 so long as there is any factual relationship between the claims joined." (Smith v. Superior Court of Alameda County 2026 WL 1876096 at *5 (cleaned up).) Plaintiff does not allege that defendants Meta and Discord engaged in a coordinated scheme, but she does allege similar derelictions regarding monitoring its platforms. (Complaint, pars. 37-39, 49-57, 60.) She also alleges that some of the same wrongdoers took advantage of her on both platforms. (Complaint, pars. 90, 100, 106.) Given this overlap and the benefits of having Plaintiff's damages from the train of abuse resolved in one case, the court concludes that joinder was proper. The court further concludes that it is not in the interests of justice to sever the claims. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 302 remotely or in person.
